subject: Performance issue on a simple mapreduce job

messages.author: f933519d8090e287
messages.subject: Performance issue on a simple mapreduce job
parts:
Hi,

I'm having a big performance issue on a simple map reduce job.
I have an hadoop cluster setup with the apache basic distribution with 4 data nodes and rmr2 3.2.0.

Here are the map and reduce functions :

mapper = function(null, line) {
  keyval(paste(line[[1]],line[[2]],line[[4]],sep="."), paste(line[[3]],line[[5]],line[[6]],line[[7]],sep="\t")  )
}

reducer = function(key, val.list) {
  library("data.table")
  library("RJSONIO")
  f = as.data.table(do.call(rbind,strsplit(unlist(val.list),split="\t")))
  f = f[!duplicated(f[,list(V1,V2,V3,V4),]),,]
  keyval(key,toJSON(f))
}

and here is how I launch it :
mapreduce(
  input="gs://av-eu-data/RESEARCH/step1",
  input.format=make.input.format(format="csv", sep = "\t"),
  output="gs://av-eu-data/RESEARCH/step2",
  output.format=make.output.format(format="csv", sep = "\t"),
  map=mapper,
  reduce=reducer,
  backend.parameters = list(hadoop = list(D="io.sort.mb=1000") )
)

The input is around 10 Gb.

When I run this job, the 162 mappers get to the end, but the 16 reducers take hours to finish. 

I've been looking on Google, but no one seems to have an issue like this. What am I doing wrong?

Thanks!
Guillaume

messages.author: 63023c771a070260
messages.subject: Re: Performance issue on a simple mapreduce job
parts:
This code is hard to follow for me, line is a data frame, are you trying to select some cols? Why paste and turn everything into strings? One suggestion is to pull the library statements out of the reducer, there is no need for those. The simplest explanation could be is that the reduce groups are really small, so the reduce function is called millions of times, and that's inefficient in R in general. I would take a look at the counters for your slow job, particularly map calls and reduce calls and maybe share them back here. Thanks


Antonio
